question: Where can I get a list of mobile network antenna sites in the United States, with location, operator and technology?

answer.summary: No official national list of mobile antenna sites with operator and technology was found. The FCC publishes two partial files: ULS Cellular-service licenses (24,366 transmitter locations with licensee, coordinates and ASR link; market-based bands list almost no sites) and the Antenna Structure Registration (142,039 standing registered structures with owner, usually a tower company, but no tenants or technology). States and cities fill gaps locally, e.g. Connecticut's Siting Council (carrier, structure owner, 5G flag; no coordinates) and city small-cell datasets.
main_caveats: ASR registers structures needing FAA notice (over 200 ft or near airports): no antennas, tenants or technology; owner is usually a tower company.
ULS site locations exist only for Cellular (CL) licenses; PCS/AWS/700 MHz market licenses are area-based and list almost no sites.
Shared sites appear once per license/call sign (ULS) or per Council action (Connecticut); deduplicate by coordinates or address.
Licensee and carrier names are historical legal entities (Cellco Partnership, New Cingular, Sprint), not current brands.
fcc.gov pages and tower company site locators (American Tower, SBA) block automated clients; data.fcc.gov bulk downloads work.
answer.confidence_reason: FCC ASR and ULS files downloaded and joined; state and city sources tested. FCC documentation was blocked (403) so field codes were inferred from data and the HIFLD schema.

attributes.note: Exact coordinates per CL transmitter location (ULS) and per registered structure (ASR); small cells only in some city datasets.
attributes.gap_note: Market-based licenses in l_market.zip have almost no LO rows (CW 1,141 rows for 7,012 licenses; AW 5 for 3,633); ASR excludes structures not needing FAA notice.

attributes.note: Licensee per CL location (ULS); carrier per siting action (Connecticut); applicant per pole (Boston).

attributes.gap_note: No national per-site LTE/5G field found in FCC files; OpenCelliD (per-cell data) requires a token and was not tested.

steps: Read HD.dat and keep license_status A.
Join EN.dat entity type L for licensee name and LO.dat for locations on the 2nd field (unique system identifier).
Convert DMS + direction to decimal degrees; deduplicate identical coordinates to approximate physical sites.
Use the ASR number in LO to join FCC ASR (r_tower.zip) for structure owner.
reading_traps: Covers only Cellular (CL) licenses; PCS, AWS, 700 MHz and other market licenses (l_market.zip) list almost no sites, so most modern antennas are absent.
Licensee names are legal entities and historical names (Cellco Partnership, New Cingular Wireless PCS, LLC, ALLTEL Corporation), not current brands.
Radio service says frequency band licensing, not LTE/5G technology.
29 of 24,366 active locations fall outside a broad US bounding box.
Field positions were matched against the HIFLD Cellular Towers schema because FCC definition documents returned 403.

steps: Keep RA status_code C with date_constructed filled and date_dismantled empty: 142,039 structures on 2026-11-22.
Join CO (coordinate_type T) and EN (entity_type O) on the unique system identifier.
reading_traps: A registered structure is not a mobile site: it may carry broadcast, paging or no mobile antennas; tenants and technology are not recorded.
Owner is the structure owner (tower companies dominate: American Towers LLC 16,821 live registrations), not the mobile operator.
66,420 of 142,039 live registrations are under 60.96 m AGL (registered for airport proximity); most short towers, rooftops and small cells elsewhere are absent.
Structure type TOWER (50,986 live) is a legacy generic code.

evidence.quote: The owner of any proposed or existing antenna structure that requires notice of proposed construction to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) due to physical obstruction must register the structure with the Commission.
